Title: [Bug]: v1.6.3 Git tag is incorrect

Body:
### Bug Summary

The v1.6.3 tag references an otherwise-dangling commit that points to out of date revisions of submodules

### Detailed Description

The v1.6.3 tag points to a dangling commit that has the wrong version of the USB library submodules, which means that users who clone and checkout the v1.6.3 tag of this repository will get an incorrect snapshot of the STM32Cube SDK.


% git log --oneline --decorate --graph origin/master v1.6.3 -5
* c7446f41 (origin/master, origin/HEAD, master) [HAL] Upload new fixes
* 878a6fd8 (HEAD) Release v1.6.3
| * bb9ba2a8 (tag: v1.6.3) Release v1.6.3
|/
* c80de4e0 [HAL] Upload new fixes
* 24d13255 [HAL] Upload new fixes

% git diff bb9ba2a8..878a6fd8
diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX
index 70a56f3d..f61249a4 160000
--- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX
+++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX
@@ -1 +1 @@
-Subproject commit 70a56f3dda1827421a443e7e5e248807293c83cc
+Subproject commit f61249a45ee3903075d2a94ce8c7c9c0c49e029d
diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library
index 555ce2b1..7b5e6886 160000
--- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library
+++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library
@@ -1 +1 @@
-Subproject commit 555ce2b1f7960031f153c93ed4e1c0bb95f34c95
+Subproject commit 7b5e6886d2f11ad15d2b46364e8a96984358f639
diff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library
index 38bc365e..9d46e44c 160000
--- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library
+++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Host_Library
@@ -1 +1 @@
-Subproject commit 38bc365e09b89c43b495af7261e31fe90a07335c
+Subproject commit 9d46e44c858a77bf126920b7bcc258d59afa89b1


Note how commit bb9ba2a8 is what's tagged as v1.6.3, but commit 878a6fd8 "Release v1.6.3" is the commit actually reachable from the master branch. The difference is in revisions of USB library submodules, and it looks like the tagged commit bb9ba2a8 is the incorrect one. Based on commit author and tag timestamps, it looks like your release engineer amended the "Release v1.6.3" commit after they already created the v1.6.3 tag, and forgot to re-create the tag on the new fixed commit before pushing to GitHub.

* STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX
  - Commit 70a56f3 is version 3.5.0 and commit f61249a is version 3.5.2
* STM32_USB_Device_Library
  - Commit 555ce2b is version 2.11.0 and commit 7b5e688 is 2.11.2
* STM32_USB_Host_Library
  - Commit 38bc365 is version 3.5.1 and commit 9d46e44 is 3.5.3

I compared this against the contents of ~/STM32Cube/Repository/STM32Cube_FW_G0_V1.6.3/Middlewares/ST/ that STM32CubeMX manages and can it looks like the official 1.6.3 release should have these newer USB library versions.

## How can this be resolved?

Either update and force-push the v1.6.3 tag to point to 878a6fd8ad440c70ee32bc6d7ad526babb6e04f4, or make a new v1.6.4 release.

title: [Bug]: [STM32CubeMX LL] "Single Sample" (ONEBIT/CR3.ONEBIT) setting has no effect — not generated for LL driver
clean_text:
Title: [Bug]: [STM32CubeMX LL] "Single Sample" (ONEBIT/CR3.ONEBIT) setting has no effect — not generated for LL driver

Body:
### Bug Summary

The "Single Sample" configuration option in CubeMX IOC has no effect when using LL drivers. No code is generated regardless of the setting, because LL_USART_InitTypeDef has no corresponding field.

### Detailed Description

CubeMX exposes a "Single Sample" option for USART/LPUART configuration which maps to the ONEBIT bit in USART_CR3. This switches the receiver from a 3-sample majority vote to 1-sample per bit.

When using HAL drivers, this setting correctly maps to UART_InitTypeDef.OneBitSampling and is generated into huart.Init.OneBitSampling = ....

When using LL drivers, LL_USART_InitTypeDef has no OneBitSampling or equivalent field. As a result:

- CubeMX generates no code for this setting regardless of the IOC value
- There is no warning or error indicating the setting was ignored
- The behavior is the same whether "Enable" or "Disable" is selected

This affects USART1, USART2, and LPUART1.

MCU/MPU Series: STM32G031 (likely all STM32 series with LL driver support)
Firmware Package: STM32Cube FW_G0
IDE: STM32CubeIDE
Driver type: LL



### Expected Behavior

LL_USART_InitTypeDef should include an OneBitSampling field and generate LL_USART_EnableOneSampling() / LL_USART_DisableOneSampling() accordingly, or CubeMX should display a warning that this setting is not supported for LL drivers and will be ignored.

### Actual Behavior

The setting is silently ignored. No code is generated and no warning is shown, leaving the developer unaware that their configuration has no effect. The hardware always uses the reset default (3-sample mode) regardless of the IOC setting.

### Environment

STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319)

### Severity

None

[KRASTM - 2026-04-15T16:08:17Z]

Thank you for the report.

Could you please share the version of CubeMx you are using and if possible, your IOC file?

With regards,

[eos1d3 - 2026-04-15T16:13:59Z]
Hi @KRASTM 

It is STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319), not using external STM32CubeMX.

This is not related to the tools because LL_USART_InitTypeDef is missing the ONEBIT bit for LL library. It does exist in HAL.

[KRASTM - 2026-04-16T15:38:40Z]
Hello @eos1d3,

After checking the documentation and referring to **RM0444 Rev 6**, the **ONEBIT / Single Sample** feature is not available for LPUART. In the register description, bit 11 is reserved and must be kept at its reset value.

For USART, this feature is disabled by default. When needed, it is enabled through the LL API:
__STATIC_INLINE void LL_USART_EnableOneBitSamp(USART_TypeDef *USARTx), inside the MX_USART1_UART_Init() function. I also tested this behavior by enabling the feature through CubeMX within STM32CubeIDE, and it works as expected.

Moreover, in the LL driver model, this configuration is not exposed in LL_USART_InitTypeDef, as LL is designed to keep the initialization lightweight and optimized.

For your information, I performed the test on Windows, not macOS. If you still encounter the issue with USART, please provide screenshots and the main.c file so we can share them with our team for further analysis. Otherwise, please allow me to close the thread.

Thank you for your understanding.

With regards

[eos1d3 - 2026-04-16T16:41:10Z]
@KRASTM 

Thank for your testing and confirmation.

For LPUART, I can confirm that the Single Sample option in MX does nothing, and LL_USART_EnableOneBitSamp is not called even it is enabled. However, the option in MX should not appear on GUI if it is not functional and is misleading a bit. 

For USART, you are right that it works as expected after further testing. MX fixes it by patching with LL_USART_EnableOneBitSamp, but not in LL_USART_Init as LL_USART_InitTypeDef completely omits the field.
This can be historical or backward compatible  issue. It is understandable.

[KRASTM - 2026-04-17T13:42:09Z]

Regarding the statement However, the option in MX should not appear on GUI if it is not functional and is misleading a bit, I see your point, and you may be right. I will share this with our team while reporting #59, as it has already been confirmed.

Title: [Bug]: [STM32CubeMX LL] LPUART1 overrun detect and DDRE settings generate inverted Enable/Disable calls

Body:
### Bug Summary

CubeMX LL code generator produces inverted function calls for LPUART1 overrun detection and DMA-deactivation-on-RX-error (DDRE). Selecting "Disabled" in the IOC generates Enable*() calls.

### Detailed Description

In the CubeMX IOC configuration for LPUART1, the "Overrun detection" and "DMA on RX error" settings produce inverted LL function calls in the generated MX_LPUART1_UART_Init():

- Setting Disabled in IOC → generates [LL_LPUART_EnableOverrunDetect(LPUART1)](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) and [LL_LPUART_EnableDMADeactOnRxErr(LPUART1)](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)
- Setting Enabled in IOC → generates no function calls at all

The same settings on USART1 and USART2 generate correct polarity (DisableOverrunDetect when Disabled is selected).

MCU/MPU Series: STM32G031
Firmware Package: STM32Cube FW_G0
IDE: STM32CubeIDE
Driver type: LL

### Expected Behavior

Selecting Disabled should generate LL_LPUART_DisableOverrunDetect() / LL_LPUART_DisableDMADeactOnRxErr() Selecting Enabled should generate LL_LPUART_EnableOverrunDetect() / LL_LPUART_EnableDMADeactOnRxErr() (or no call, since enabled is the reset default)

### Actual Behavior

Polarity is inverted for LPUART1 only — Disabled generates Enable calls. The hardware reset default for both settings is enabled, so with "Enabled" in the IOC generating no code, the actual hardware state happens to be correct by accident. However, selecting "Disabled" silently enables overrun detection instead of disabling it.

### Environment

STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319)

### Severity

None

Body:
### Bug Summary

CubeMX generates incorrect default values for BaudRate and DataWidth in MX_LPUART1_UART_Init() when using LL drivers on STM32G0 series.

### Detailed Description

When adding LPUART1 to a new STM32G0 project with LL driver selection in CubeMX, the generated LL_LPUART_InitTypeDef struct is populated with incorrect defaults even before the user configures the peripheral:

- BaudRate is generated as a nonstandard value (observed: 209700) instead of a standard baud rate
- DataWidth is generated as LL_LPUART_DATAWIDTH_7B instead of LL_LPUART_DATAWIDTH_8B

These incorrect defaults do not occur for USART1 or USART2 — only LPUART1 is affected.

MCU/MPU Series: STM32G031
Firmware Package: STM32Cube FW_G0
IDE: STM32CubeIDE
Driver type: LL

### Expected Behavior

Generated code should default to BaudRate = 115200 and DataWidth = LL_LPUART_DATAWIDTH_8B, consistent with USART1/USART2 LL generation behavior.

### Actual Behavior

Generated code contains BaudRate = 209700 and DataWidth = LL_LPUART_DATAWIDTH_7B, which produce incorrect UART operation at runtime.

### Environment

STM32CubeIDE 1.19.0, macOS 14.8.4 (23J319)

### Severity

Major

title: STM32G0 HAL UART IRQ Handler Missing IDLE Event Handling in DMA Circular Mode
clean_text:
Title: STM32G0 HAL UART IRQ Handler Missing IDLE Event Handling in DMA Circular Mode

Body:
## Issue Description

### Problem Summary
There is a functional inconsistency between the STM32G0 and STM32H7 series HAL libraries in the [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) implementation. Specifically, the STM32G0 version lacks the logic to handle IDLE events in DMA circular mode, which can lead to improper event notification to the application layer under certain usage scenarios.

### Detailed Description

1. **Inconsistent DMA Circular Mode Checking Approach**:
   - STM32G0 uses [HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(huart->hdmarx->Instance->CCR, DMA_CCR_CIRC)](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Openlib\perf_counter\CI\perf_counter_template_gcc\Drivers\STM32F1xx_HAL_Driver\Inc\stm32f1xx_hal_def.h#L59-L60)
   - STM32H7 uses huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode != DMA_CIRCULAR

2. **Missing IDLE Event Handling in Circular Mode**:
   The STM32H7 version includes the following logic in [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) that is missing in the STM32G0 version:
   c
   /* If DMA is in Circular mode, Idle event is to be reported to user
      even if occurring after a Transfer Complete event from DMA */
   if (nb_remaining_rx_data == huart->RxXferSize)
   {
     if (huart->hdmarx->Init.Mode == DMA_CIRCULAR)
     {
       /* Initialize type of RxEvent that correspond to RxEvent callback execution;
          In this case, Rx Event type is Idle Event */
       huart->RxEventType = HAL_UART_RXEVENT_IDLE;
       // Callback invocation
     }
   }
   


### Impact
When using DMA circular mode for UART reception, if an IDLE line event occurs after the reception buffer is filled, the STM32G0 version will not notify the application layer. This may result in delayed data processing or missed event notifications.

### Expected Fix
It is recommended to unify the [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627) implementation between STM32G0 and STM32H7 series, enhancing the STM32G0 version's functional completeness to ensure consistent behavior across all usage scenarios. This would involve:
1. Standardizing the DMA circular mode detection method
2. Adding the missing IDLE event handling logic for circular mode operation

### Environment
- MCU Series: STM32G0
- HAL Library Version: [Please specify version]
- Affected Module: UART HAL driver ([stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c))
- Function: [HAL_UART_IRQHandler](file://D:\work\2025FLUX\flux_temp\temp_10_20_485\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal_uart.c#L2304-L2627)

title: PREFETCH_ENABLE not implemented
clean_text:
Title: PREFETCH_ENABLE not implemented

Body:
In STM32G0xx_hal_conf.h, these macros are defined:

#define  VDD_VALUE                    (3300UL)                                        /*!< Value of VDD in mv */
#define  TICK_INT_PRIORITY            0U /*!< tick interrupt priority */
#define  USE_RTOS                     0U
#define  PREFETCH_ENABLE              0U
#define  INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE     1U

As far as I can tell, PREFETCH_ENABLE is not implemented and has no affect on any of the library code. In order to disable prefetch we had to add the following in our main.c after SystemClock_Config():

  // CRITICAL: Explicitly disable prefetch for STM32G0 errata 2.2.10
  // The PREFETCH_ENABLE define in hal_conf.h is NOT used by the HAL
  // We must manually clear the PRFTEN bit in FLASH->ACR
  // Confirm that prefetch is not disabled by setting PREFETCH_ENABLE to 0
  if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN) != 0) {
    CLEAR_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN);
  }
  
  // Verify prefetch is actually disabled
  if (READ_BIT(FLASH->ACR, FLASH_ACR_PRFTEN) != 0) {
    // Prefetch failed to disable - this should never happen
    Error_Handler();
  }

As noted in my comment above, this directly addresses the "silicon bug" described in errata 2.2.10, as anyone attempting to disable prefetch in the CubeMX/IDE GUI may not realize that doing this in the gui (or the header) has no effect. 

We fought random hardfaults for 2 months to no avail until we discovered this bug, and lost an hour or so not realizing that we had to manually disable prefetch with the above code. 

For what it's worth, I'm not sure INSTRUCTION_CACHE_ENABLE is implemented either.

Comments:

In:
STM32Cube_FW_G0\Drivers\STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver\Src\stm32g0xx_hal.c
HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_Init(void)
#if (PREFETCH_ENABLE != 0U)
  __HAL_FLASH_PREFETCH_BUFFER_ENABLE();
#endif /* PREFETCH_ENABLE */

[IMAGE ATTACHED]

[IMAGE ATTACHED]

So Prefetch enable shouldn't need an explicit disable if RM0444 Rev 6 is correct on reset behavior.  To be clear, are you seeing prefetch enable bit set after reset?  Are you writing to FLASH->ACR elsewhere in the code?

title: USBPD Analyzer often lags with I2C timeout
clean_text:
Title: USBPD Analyzer often lags with I2C timeout

Body:
Two FreeRTOS threads call at least BSP_PWRMON_GetVoltage() without locking I2C by a mutex.
When another I2C operation is re-entered while the first one is not finished, I2C fails and waits till 3 sec timeout.
Mainly happens at https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/blob/fcc63f394b69d25d005c431be60960d2c22acab8/Projects/STM32G071B-DISCO/Demonstrations/USBPD_Analyzer/Src/demo_disco.c#L1347

Mutex guarded version BSP_USBPD_PWR_VBUSGetVoltage() should be used instead of BSP_PWRMON_GetVoltage(ALERT_VBUS, ...).
Similarly BSP_USBPD_PWR_VBUSGetCurrent() should replace BSP_PWRMON_GetCurrent(ALERT_VBUS, ...).
Also other I2C should be guarded similarly, e.g. BSP_PWRMON_GetVoltage(ALERT_CC1 / ALERT_CC2 ...) but there is no direct replacement in BSP_USBPD_PWR_ module.

title: not usefull const in stm32g0xx_ll_dma.h
clean_text:
Title: not usefull const in stm32g0xx_ll_dma.h

Body:
const is one of the importers keywords in C/C++.
It is great, that you add more and more const.

Const tell the compiler, that the symbol is not writable.

For example,
Get function should set const for the object
Set function should not set const for the object

But now you add const to object that are modified.

For example,
__STATIC_INLINE void LL_DMA_EnableChannel(const DMA_TypeDef *DMAx, uint32_t Channel)
{
  uint32_t dma_base_addr = (uint32_t)DMAx;
  SET_BIT(((DMA_Channel_TypeDef *)(dma_base_addr + CHANNEL_OFFSET_TAB[Channel]))->CCR, DMA_CCR_EN);
}

This function modifies *DMAx. So DMAx should not be const.

Here it works because you cast DMAx to a uint32_t and so you lost the const attribute.
Casting is always a dangerous modification!

Please remove const from DMA_TypeDef *DMAx in the following functions
LL_DMA_EnableChannel()
LL_DMA_DisableChannel()
LL_DMA_ConfigTransfer()
LL_DMA_SetDataTransferDirection()
LL_DMA_SetMode()
LL_DMA_SetPeriphIncMode()
LL_DMA_SetMemoryIncMode()
LL_DMA_SetMemoryIncMode()
LL_DMA_SetMemorySize()
LL_DMA_SetChannelPriorityLevel()
LL_DMA_SetDataLength()
LL_DMA_ConfigAddresses()
LL_DMA_SetMemoryAddress()
LL_DMA_SetPeriphAddress()
LL_DMA_SetM2MSrcAddress()
LL_DMA_SetM2MDstAddress()
LL_DMA_SetPeriphRequest ()
LL_DMA_EnableIT_TC ()
LL_DMA_EnableIT_HT()

Title: Lint suppressions in FreeRTOS have a trailing full-stop character which pc-lint rejects

Body:
**Setup**

We're working on a project that includes both an STM32G0 and and STM32L4+ MCU. We are using FreeRTOS on both boards. We build with CubeIDE 1.14.0.

We are getting our FreeRTOS source code from this repository rather than the one provided by CubeIDE. We are using release 1.6.1 of this repo.

We use pc-lint v1.4.1 to run static analysis on both of our projects.

**Bug description**

The FreeRTOS source includes lines like the following, in Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/tasks.c:


#undef MPU_WRAPPERS_INCLUDED_FROM_API_FILE /*lint !e961 !e750 !e9021. */


This is rejected by pc-lint, as follows:


Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/tasks.c 47:44 error 72: bad option '!e9021.': invalid message number for !e

We have determined that it is the full-stop at the end of !e9021. that causes the problem. If we remove the full-stop, lint works as expected.

The same issue is in other source files too: stream_buffer.c, timers.c, queue.c.

**Other notes**

I've submitted this bug report in the STM32CubeG0 repo, but I suspect it exists for other flavours of STM32 too. It's certainly also a problem on the STM32L4+ repo.

**Describe the set-up**

 *  Use I2C1 or I2C2 to communicate with CAT24C02TDI EEPROM memory

**Describe the bug**

When checking an I2C device, the check function HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() may return an error, even if the I2C device is OK.

The _STM32Cube FW_G0 V1.6.1_ does not have such problem.

**How To Reproduce**

Call the HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() function several times:

HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady(eeprom->hi2c, eeprom->dev_addr, 100, 200);


**Additional context**

Supposedly, the problem is in I2C_IsErrorOccurred() function.

If the next condition is true:

  if (HAL_IS_BIT_SET(itflag, I2C_FLAG_AF))

the next code will always be executed:

    error_code |= HAL_I2C_ERROR_AF;

    status = HAL_ERROR;

And then the I2C_IsErrorOccurred() function will fail.

![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/assets/14815310/3631819b-bb1f-49e1-aeb3-bb83d8ac1f6a)

**Describe the bug**

This can be achieved by polling/waiting for LL_ADC_IsActiveFlag_ADRDY(hadc->Instance) to return true, although this doesn't apply a timeout, so could end in deadlock. A polled solution with a timeout should be implemented, as used elsewhere in this function.

**How To Reproduce**

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).

Calling HAL_ADCEx_Calibration_Start()

**Additional context**

[insolace - 2025-06-23T22:03:10Z]
Sorry to reopen an old issue, but the fix to this problem assumes that the ADC is using the system clock. If RCC.ADCCLockSelection=RCC_ADCCLKSOURCE_HSI and the prescaller is DIV4, then the delay is not applied and the ADC fails to run.

See line 179 of stm32g0xx_hal_adc_ex.c:

if (adc_clk_async_presc >= LL_ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV16)

[JakubVanek - 2025-07-13T21:43:45Z]
Hello, I can confirm the issue in a slightly different configuration. About a year ago I was working on a device with a STM32G0B1 with the following clock setup:
- The system uses a 8 MHz crystal.
- The CPU runs at 64 MHz and is clocked by the PLL.
- The ADC runs at 8 MHz and the 8 MHz clock is directly provided by the PLL (not by the ADC-internal prescaler).
- The ADC is configured with ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV1.
- IIRC the reason for this somewhat weird clock setup was that we needed longer sampling times and these were not available when the ADC was clocked synchronously from APB.


Under these conditions the fix implemented in STM32 HAL did not work for me. I had to replace the block in

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32g0xx-hal-driver/blob/b86a4ee8d730b2c1696416048ca4b4f3f31d8c04/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_adc_ex.c#L175-L192

with an application-specific workaround:

c
// JakubVanek: adding the delay below. Without this, firmware with -Os build config
// puts the ADC into a weird state with permanent ADEN=1 and ADDIS=1.
for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) { // a minimum of 9 worked, 32 should be a safe bet
    __NOP();
}

[insolace - 2025-11-19T00:31:35Z]
This really needs to be reopened. 

stm32g0xx_hal_adc_ex.c:179:

if (adc_clk_async_presc >= LL_ADC_CLOCK_ASYNC_DIV16)

STM32G0B1RET datasheet says that the maximum ADC clock allowed must be <= 35MHz. The current version of STM32CubeMX throws errors if you select a clock source above this, even if you use a prescaler that results in a speed lower than this. The implication is that the clock before the prescaler matters, and I've been chasing hard fault issues because we needed a 4MHz clock at the only way to get it to work with the current driver was to use sysclk = 64mhz and a prescaler of async 16. 

To get a 4MHz clock in STM32 Cube MX without getting a warning, we have to set PLLP to 32MHz and use a prescaler of 8. This fails the above check and skips the delay, which causes the ADC to fail calibration and not work.

For now we're having to remove the prescaler check and force the delay. This code gets overwritten anytime cubemx generates code, which we can handle, but this will cause a huge headache for future users during bringup.

I2C addr flag not reset inside I2C_ITAddrCplt

Title: I2C addr flag not reset inside I2C_ITAddrCplt

Body:
Inside I2C_ITAddrCplt the address flag is reset for
- 10bit mode (if event count == 2)
- listen is disabled

it is **not reset** for 
- 7bit mode
- 10bit mode (if event count == 1)

See
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/blob/03cb8e9ec0cbefad623caebe47359df0bab1d05e/Drivers/STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32g0xx_hal_i2c.c#L5486

I think this is an error, it should be reset in all cases before calling HAL_I2C_AddrCallback(hi2c, transferdirection, slaveaddrcode);. This means HAL_I2C_CLEAR_FLAG(hi2c, I2C_FLAG_ADDR); should be added in the two cases mentioned above.
If the flag is not reset, the chip will pull the clock line low forever after receiving its slave address.

Body:
**Set-up**
 * NUCLEO-G0B1RE
 * STM32CubeMX with Makefile selected as Toolchain / IDE

**Description**
When setting up a USB-PD project – STM32CubeMX does not generate the needed static library imports in the Makefile, causing a lot of undefined reference errors when compiling. These references are impossible to look up due to them being defined in archived libraries, making it impossible to debug.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Set up a new project in STMCubeMX according to [AN5418](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/dm00663511-how-to-build-a-simple-usbpd-sink-application-with-stm32cubemx-stmicroelectronics.pdf).

2. Choose Makefile as Toolchain / IDE in the Project Manager tab.

3. Generate the code and build with $ make

4. Observe failed build caused by undefined reference errors in the output.

**Solution**
The error is caused by missing static library definitions in the generated Makefile.

*Generated Makefile:*

Makefile
# libraries
LIBS = -lc -lm -lnosys 
LIBDIR = 
LDFLAGS = $(MCU) -specs=nano.specs -T$(LDSCRIPT) $(LIBDIR) $(LIBS) -Wl,-Map=$(BUILD_DIR)/$(TARGET).map,--cref -Wl,--gc-sections


*Expected Makefile:*

Makefile
# libraries
LIBS = -lc -lm -lnosys 
LIBDIR = Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Core/lib/USBPDCORE_PD3_FULL_CM0PLUS_wc32.a
LDFLAGS = $(MCU) -specs=nano.specs -T$(LDSCRIPT) $(LIBDIR) $(LIBS) -Wl,-Map=$(BUILD_DIR)/$(TARGET).map,--cref -Wl,--gc-sections


Observe change in LIBDIR.  
The static library is chosen by selecting a Stack Configuration for the USBPD middleware in STM32CubeMX.  
Correct behaviour can be seen when doing the exact same project setup inside STM32CubeIDE.

Details:

![Screenshot_2021-09-25_09-35-04](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79528/134758248-f56eea12-964f-4f66-a7de-eb56ede3fcc5.png)

These screenshots show that the Slave is unable to handle Data read requests from the Master I2C device.

The Slave returned data is always 0xFF. I saw https://www.i2c-bus.org/i2c-primer/analysing-obscure-problems/data-bytes-from-slave-are-0xff/ on this topic.

The I2 Master device is Arduino Pro Mini ATMega328P running @ 8 MHz @ 3.3v.

I2C2 global interrupt is enabled in my STM32CubeIDE project.

![Screenshot_2021-09-25_10-05-46](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79528/134758276-f24ca236-ae13-41ce-9037-23593a90191e.png)

Note: In comparison, when I run a similar STM32CubeIDE project on my STM32F103C8T6  "Blue Pill" board, things just work well as expected (Slave is able to send back actual data).

I am attaching the source code for the I2C Master and I2C Slave (STM32G031J6) below:

- [i2c_slave_code.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/files/7229160/i2c_slave_code.zip)
- [master.ino.txt](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeG0/files/7229159/master.ino.txt)

- Is there a reason why the STM32G0316-DISCO board software package has no I2C examples? They will be super helpful for users.

What further information may I provide for debugging this problem? Thanks for your help! :)

title: __RAM_FUNC breaks when inlined by GCC LTO
clean_text:
Title: __RAM_FUNC breaks when inlined by GCC LTO

Body:
When GCC inlines functions, it ignores the section attribute of the inlined function. (This seems to be considered a feature, not a bug: https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=31362, https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=78903, etc)

Drivers/STM32G0xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32g0xx_hal_def.h has:

#define __RAM_FUNC __attribute__((section(".RamFunc")))

This is used by FLASH_Program_Fast in stm32g0xx_hal_flash.c (which must run from RAM because it needs exclusive access to flash).

When compiling with LTO, GCC will inline functions across different source files. That means FLASH_Program_Fast may be inlined into the application code that calls it, which is typically not in .RamFunc, so the code will run from flash and will fail.

I believe the best way to fix this is with noinline, i.e.

#define __RAM_FUNC __attribute__((section(".RamFunc"), noinline))

Then the function won't be inlined and will remain in the correct section.

(With this change, I was able to successfully build my code with LTO (which significantly reduces code size) and haven't noticed any other problems.)

#ifdef __cplusplus

#endif

#include "stm32g0xx_ll_usb.h"

#if defined (USB_DRD_FS)


... The rest of the code  ...


#endif /* defined (USB_DRD_FS) */

Title: STM32G0 HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback() incompatibility

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
- Nucleo F746
- CubeIDE 1.3.0
- HAL FW G0 v1.3.0

**Describe the bug**
The following call back should be called when EXTI is accepted, according to the HAL reference UM2319 - Rev 1, section 3.11 : 

 void HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback(uint16_t GPIO_Pin)
{
}

This is common manner among the STM32 series. 

But only STM32G0 uses HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Rising_Callback() and HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Falling_Callback().

This is a bad idea to make a Hardware "Abstraction" Layer. The API should be aligned among the different hardware, as far as possible. ANd this is a possible case. 

**How To Reproduce**
 1. The demo program turn on the LED on the HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback.
 1. Clone the [stm32-defects repository](https://github.com/suikan4github/stm32-defects). 
 1. Import d003-nucleo-g070-gpio-exti into CubeIDE
 1. Build and run the project on the Nucleo-G070. 
 1. Import d003-nucleo-g431rb-control into CubeIDE
 1. BUild and run the project on the Nucleo-G431RB.

Please push the blue button (B1) of the Nucleo. On the Nucleo G070, the green LED is off, while the Nucleo G431RB the green LED in turned on. Both projects try to catch the EXTI by HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback() and turn on LED. The G431RB is expected behavior. 

**Additional context**
This is duplicated with the [bug-report on the community](https://community.st.com/s/question/0D50X0000C6eVvdSQE/stm32g0-hal-exti-callback-implementation-is-buggy).

Title: VBUS race condition where USB TypeC 'attach' event is never seen by the application

Body:
**Overview**
Possible issue in the Middleware USB-PD G0 Device section

**Describe the set-up**
 * Custom board where BSP_PWR_VBUSGetVoltage() senses TypeC voltage.
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc (GNU Tools for Arm Embedded Processors 7-2018-q2-update) 7.3.1 20180622 (release) [ARM/embedded-7-branch revision 261907]

**Describe the bug**
Possible issue in USB PD Middleware Device for G0. At attach sensing time, the library should check for VBUS to stabilize to Vsafe5V before moving forward. However, I believe there's an incorrect conditional for this check.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Have a system with relatively fast VBUS ramp (less than CAD_TPDDEBOUCE_THRESHOLD)
2. Attached a USB PD compliant device
3. No attach event occurs.

**Additional context**
This patch gets me past this issue.

iff --git a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_cad_hw_if.c b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_cad_hw_if.c
index 0209bb8..3068df8 100644
--- a/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_cad_hw_if.c
+++ b/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USBPD_Library/Devices/STM32G0XX/src/usbpd_cad_hw_if.c
@@ -766,7 +766,7 @@ static uint32_t ManageStateAttachedWait_SRC(uint8_t PortNum, USBPD_CAD_EVENT *pE
   
   if ((_handle->CurrentHWcondition != HW_Detachment) && (_handle->CurrentHWcondition != HW_PwrCable_NoSink_Attachment))
   {
-    if ((BSP_PWR_VBUSGetVoltage(PortNum) > BSP_PWR_LOW_VBUS_THRESHOLD)
+    if ((BSP_PWR_VBUSGetVoltage(PortNum) < BSP_PWR_LOW_VBUS_THRESHOLD)^M
         && (USBPD_PORTPOWERROLE_SRC == Ports[PortNum].params->PE_PowerRole))
     {
       /* reset the timing because VBUS threshold not yet reach */

title: Consistent RCC definitions
clean_text:
Title: Consistent RCC definitions

Body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * arm-none-eabi-gcc
 * #include <stm32g0xx.h>

**Describe the bug**

There are a few definitions missing that are available on all other devices with the same RCC implementation. This is annoying when you need to maintain a family independent RCC HAL.

- RCC_CFGR_HPRE_DIV*:  All STM32 devices
- RCC_CFGR_SW_*: All STM32 devices
- RCC_CFGR_PPRE_DIV*: Only F0, G0 devices

**How To Reproduce**

Try to use RCC_CFGR_HPRE_DIV1 or RCC_CFGR_PPRE_DIV1 or RCC_CFGR_SW_HSI in any code that includes the STM32G0 header.

**Additional context**

Patches:
- [RCC_CFGR_HPRE_DIV*](https://github.com/modm-io/cmsis-header-stm32/blob/master/patches/g0-2.patch)
- [RCC_CFGR_SW_*](https://github.com/modm-io/cmsis-header-stm32/blob/master/patches/g0.patch)
- [RCC_CFGR_PPRE_DIV*](https://github.com/modm-io/cmsis-header-stm32/blob/master/patches/g0-3.patch)

The specific use of [these missing defines in our code](https://github.com/modm-io/modm/blob/develop/src/modm/platform/clock/stm32/rcc.hpp.in#L78-L162).

Comments:
[CCASTM - 2019-06-05T09:01:18Z]
Hello Niklas,
Thank you for your remark.
We will analyze it and come back to you.
Regards
Christophe

[ALABSTM - 2019-06-27T08:56:57Z]
Hi Niklas,

After reporting this issue to the technical committee the decision taken is to **remove these definitions from the CMSIS**. In fact, they are not the standard bit definitions recommended by Arm to be in the CMSIS.

Moreover as these constants are defined in the CMSIS, they are strictly meant to be used by the HAL and LL drivers, not the user-application code.
Instead the user-application code is meant to use the following **redefinitions** present in **hal_rcc.h** and **ll_rcc.h**:
- RCC_SYSCLK_DIV*
- RCC_HCLK_DIV*
- RCC_SYSCLKSOURCE_STATUS_*

Actually, what you found on G0 and F0 is the fix that has been applied on these two firmwares. It is how things should be. The same fix still needs to be applied on the other firmwares.

These constants shall have not been defined in the CMSIS file. We do apologize for the inconvenience incurred.

With regards

[ALABSTM - 2019-06-27T08:57:57Z]
ST Internal Reference: 84151

[salkinium - 2019-06-27T14:43:17Z]
My understanding this from a technical point is that you as a vendor specify the CMSIS SVD and then use a converter (officially SVDConv.exe, but your headers seem manually edited too) to create the CMSIS header files in C.

The [CMSIS SVD format **explicitly** describes enumerated value levels](http://www.keil.com/pack/doc/CMSIS/SVD/html/elem_registers.html#elem_enumeratedValues). (Ironically the example they use is of clock sources ;-) They are supposed to be used exactly for specifing the **meaning** of the bit fields.

Looking at your CMSIS-SVD files for the series, I find no such value level enumerations for the [register RCC->CFGR](https://github.com/posborne/cmsis-svd/blob/master/data/STMicro/STM32G07x.svd#L1210-L1263) (or any other register for that matter):
xml
            <field>
              <name>HPRE</name>
              <description>AHB prescaler</description>
              <bitOffset>8</bitOffset>
              <bitWidth>4</bitWidth>
              <access>read-write</access>
            </field>


I've looked again at the header files, and indeed, they are completely consistent in that regard, there are only _Msk and _Pos values, and they reflect what is defined in the SVD file.

I think it's fine to **be consistent** about where you define what, however, PLEASE give use a machine-readable list of enumerations. The CMSIS-SVD files provide you the perfect mechanism to do so.

I hope you understand that there is considerable research being done for making embedded software more safe and secure, incl. by the Ada and Rust community. They rely on the SVD files to generate the appropriate language definition to access the registers and **the lack of enumeration values is a significant burden.**

There is a giant manual effort to **fix and add** the missing definitions by the Rust community:
https://github.com/stm32-rs/stm32-rs

Note in particular the **big set of patches** of your SVD files:
https://github.com/stm32-rs/stm32-rs/tree/master/peripherals

You should incorporate them into your own, so that **YOU** benefit from these corrections too. (This isn't just a one-way street, your own engineers may also be using these wrong definitions).

Please relay this to the technical commitee, so they can understand why this information is important and how you can improve your own software. **This is important to a whole lot of embedded developers.**

#define DMAMUX1_IdRegisters        ((DMAMUX_IdRegisters_TypeDef *) DMAMUX1_IdRegisters_BASE)

#define STM32G071xx 1

DMAMUX_IdRegisters_TypeDef type;
